text:
The diff raises the OSPF cost from 10 to 65535 on one interface each of PAO and SEA. The two routers appear to share a link (SEA-PAO), so the change effectively de-prefers that link. The adjacency should remain up, traffic should shift to alternate paths, and reachability should be unchanged. The tests below check that and probe the main risks (convergence, load on the alternate paths, and loss of connectivity).
